description:
FOUND by a2775 (s510) when the trial removal of join's call-wide `(p-list-ctx (p-join ...))` bind (#2775, variant 3) made perl-tests/hashassign.t row 'hash assignment in list context removes duplicates' (`join ':', %h = (1) x 8`) answer 8 instead of 1:1 -- the sweep's only NEW row (/home/bernt/pcl/.claude/worktrees/agent-a24e9cbaab6227172/scratch/a2775/sweep-v3.log).

CAUSE: Pl/ExprToCL.pm's `%h = ...` arm (~line 1562 at 597a2bd4) binds `(p-list-ctx/p-scalar-ctx (p-hash-= ...))` by the node's context ONLY when the RHS node is a tree_val/progn (a literal list); any other RHS shape (a repetition `x`, a call, an array) falls through to the generic path, emitted bare, and p-hash-= reads whatever *wantarray* the surroundings left (`(eq *wantarray* t)`).  Probes /home/bernt/pcl/.claude/worktrees/agent-a24e9cbaab6227172/scratch/a2775/pj.pl, /home/bernt/pcl/.claude/worktrees/agent-a24e9cbaab6227172/scratch/a2775/pj2.pl vs perl 5.40.3 on main: `print %h = (1) x 8` -> 8 (perl 11); `push my @y, %h = (3) x 4` -> 1 (perl 2); inside join it is right only because of join's call-wide bind.

CONSEQUENCE FOR #2775: join's bind is NOT redundant for correctness (its comment, citing #2004, is wrong for this shape).  Fix this first (bind the hash assignment by its node context for every RHS shape -- the array/list assignment arms are the model), then join's bind can go with the fallback.  Guard rows: the three pj2.pl lines + the join line of pj.pl.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a HASH assignment whose RHS is not a literal list (`%h = (1) x 8`) carries no context bind of its own -- in a LIST slot it answers the scalar count: `print %h = (1) x 8` prints 8 (perl 11), `push @y, %h = (3) x 4` pushes 1 value (perl 2); join's call-wide bind hides it inside join only
